h1:
Cafes + Old Town
on the Chanthaboon Waterfront, 2 Days
intro: The Chanthaboon Waterfront is Chanthaburi's oldest street, running about 900 meters along the Chanthaburi River and lined with Sino-European shophouses close to 300 years old. Over the past few years a wave of new-generation cafes has opened inside those old buildings, so you can easily spend a whole day wandering here. This is a 2-day plan that pulls cafe-hopping, old-town architecture, a walk across the bridge to the cathedral, and Chanthaburi's local dishes into one trip.

blocks.html: This trip suits people who like to wander slowly, photograph old buildings, sit in cafes with a coffee, and not drive much, because all the main sights are within walking distance of each other around the Chanthaboon Waterfront. We set day one for walking the full length of Sukhaphiban Road with stops at the standout cafes, and day two for crossing the bridge to the cathedral and picking up local food and souvenirs before heading home.

blocks.text: A few things to know before you go

items: Parking — Sukhaphiban Road through the community is narrow and hard for cars to pass each other. It's best to park near a temple lot or on an outer street and walk in.
Best timing — Most cafes open around 9:00 AM–6:00 PM, and several close on certain weekdays. Saturdays and Sundays have more places open but bigger crowds.
What to wear — If you plan to enter the cathedral, dress modestly and cover your shoulders, since it's a sacred place still used for actual services.
Carry cash — Many small shops in the community take only cash or bank transfer.

items.label: Day trips from Chanthaburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 1 — Walk Sukhaphiban Road + cafes in old shophouses

blocks.html: Day one is about walking the full Chanthaboon Waterfront. This street was once the trading quarter of Chinese and Vietnamese immigrants, so the shophouses on both sides blend Chinese-European styles with old fretwork timber houses. Walk slowly and you can drift between cafes and souvenir shops the whole way.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Walk the old town + waterfront cafe crawl

items.activity: Start at the top of Sukhaphiban Road and walk into the Chanthaboon Waterfront
items.note: Photograph the community sign and the old buildings in the morning before the sun gets harsh and while it's still quiet.

The shop that revived Chanthaburi's forgotten local coffee varietal. Signature drinks are Chan Phong and Mapid Chantra (coffee mixed with Chanthaburi's mapid kumquat), around 120 THB. Boards around the shop tell the story of Chanthaburi coffee.

items.activity: Walk on and visit the House No. 69 Learning Center
items.note: An old house opened as a space telling the story of riverside life in the past. You can go in and see old household objects and photographs.

items.activity: Lunch in the community — kuay jub or tom yum seafood noodles
items.note: The community has several spots doing kuay jub and tom yum noodles with fresh seafood. Eat light and save room for more cafes.

items.activity: Relax at Chong Dee by C.A.P, in a near-century-old house
items.note: A cafe in a restored old Chinese building. Recommended is Cheng Tueng Coffee, served with traditional Chinese sweets, around 120 THB. Cool, shaded atmosphere right by the river.

items.activity: Switch to BRB.coffee, a small specialty coffee shop
items.note: For those who like black coffee that highlights the bean, this place has both house blend and single origin. Americano starts around 70 THB. A good afternoon sip.

items.activity: Walk back along the end of the street, catching the evening light by the river
items.note: The late light is soft, and the old buildings against the river photograph beautifully. Stop at the little souvenir shops along the way.

items.activity: Dinner: Sen Chan stir-fried with crab, a Chanthaburi classic
items.note: The long-running Sen Chan crab noodle shops are both in town and near the community. The chewy noodles are stir-fried with fresh crab in a sweet-sour sauce, one dish worth trying at least once.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Don't try to hit every cafe in one go, because several cups back to back will fill you up fast. Pick 2–3 places you really want to sit at, then alternate with walks past the old buildings, it's more fun that way.

Day two, cross the Niramol Bridge to the cathedral side, a Chanthaburi landmark, then loop back to a riverside cafe on the community side late morning before picking up Chanthaburi souvenirs like pepper and dried seafood for the trip home.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: See the church + a river-view cafe + souvenir shopping

items.activity: Cross the Niramol Bridge to the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
items.note: The largest Christian church in Thailand, built in Gothic style with golden teak columns and stained glass. Free entry, open around 9:00 AM–3:00 PM. Dress modestly.

items.activity: Stroll around the church, photographing the clock tower and the canalside
items.note: The spot in front of the church with the bridge is a popular photo angle. Late morning the light hits the facade just right.

items.activity: Cross back for a river-view cafe on the community side, such as Thammada Rimnam Chanthaburi
items.note: The cafe has a riverside seating zone and a resident cat. The signature is Dirty Coffee, around 120 THB, plus a butterfly-pea mapid. An easy spot to catch the river breeze.

items.activity: Lunch: seafood or noodles by the river
items.note: Pick a riverside restaurant in the community with fresh seafood. A nice closing meal before souvenir shopping.

items.activity: Stop at KAWA Matcha for the green-tea fans
items.note: A dedicated matcha cafe in the community. Signature is the Matcha Mousse Cake, around 120 THB, with a strong, clear tea flavor. A good way to finish with something sweet.

items.activity: Pick up Chanthaburi souvenirs — pepper, dried seafood, fried durian
items.note: Fragrant Chanthaburi pepper is a well-known souvenir, found at shops in town and at the markets. Dried seafood and fried durian are popular too.
If you have time left, drop by a market in town or grab one last cup of coffee before leaving Chanthaburi.

blocks.text: Standout cafes on the Chanthaboon Waterfront

blocks.html: If you'd rather pick your own places by style, here are the cafes in and around the community that people talk about and that are actually open, covering specialty coffee, matcha, and easy riverside seats.

items.name: The Chanthaboon Coffee
items.blurb: The heart of the quarter, the shop that brought back Chanthaburi's local coffee varietal after it was forgotten for over 170 years. Boards around the shop tell the story of Chanthaburi coffee. Signature drinks are Chan Phong and Mapid Chantra.
items.meta: Specialty coffee · tells the city's story

items.name: Chong Dee by C.A.P
items.blurb: A cafe in a restored, near-century-old Chinese house with a cool, shaded riverside feel. The signature is Cheng Tueng Coffee, served with traditional Chinese sweets.
items.meta: Cafe in an old building · riverside

items.name: Thammada Rimnam Chanthaburi
items.blurb: A cafe and eatery with a riverside seating zone and a resident cat to play with. Signature drinks are Dirty Coffee and a butterfly-pea mapid. An easy spot to catch the river breeze.

items.name: BRB.coffee
items.blurb: A small, pared-back specialty coffee shop with both house blend and single origin, ideal for black-coffee drinkers who want to taste the bean. There are oat milk and matcha options too.

items.name: KAWA Matcha
items.blurb: A dedicated matcha cafe for green-tea fans. The signature is the Matcha Mousse Cake with a strong, clear tea flavor, a good place to finish with something sweet.

items.name: Choen Rimnam Chanthaboon by Have A Seat
items.blurb: A cafe and restaurant in the old riverside community where you can sit for a coffee or a light meal. The feel is simple and warm, in the style of an old house.

blocks.title: How to choose a place
blocks.html: If you only have one day and can pick a couple of spots, start with The Chanthaboon Coffee to understand the story of Chanthaburi coffee, then follow it with a riverside cafe to catch the river view. That way you get both the story and the atmosphere in one trip.

items.name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
items.blurb: The largest Gothic Christian church in Thailand, just across from the community. Cross the Niramol Bridge to reach it. Free entry.

items.name: House No. 69 Learning Center
items.blurb: An old house in the community displaying the way of life and stories of riverside people in the past. Drop in while walking Sukhaphiban Road.

items.name: Niramol Bridge
items.blurb: The bridge across the river linking the community to the church side. A photo spot for river views with the old buildings.

faq.q: How long does it take to walk the Chanthaboon Waterfront?
faq.a: If you just walk straight through it takes about an hour, since the street is roughly 900 meters long. But if you stop at cafes, photograph the old buildings, and visit the learning center, set aside half a day to a full day so you can take it slow.

faq.q: What hours do the cafes on the Chanthaboon Waterfront keep?
faq.a: Most open around 9:00 AM–6:00 PM, and each place has different closing days, with some shut on certain weekdays. Saturdays and Sundays have more places open. It's worth checking each shop's page before you go to be sure.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for the cathedral?
faq.a: Entry is free, open for visits around 9:00 AM–3:00 PM. Since it's still used for actual services, dress modestly, cover your shoulders, and be respectful while inside.

faq.q: What Chanthaburi souvenirs are worth bringing back?
faq.a: Fragrant Chanthaburi pepper is one of the top-known souvenirs, followed by dried seafood, fried durian, and processed fruit. You can find them at shops in town and at the markets.

faq.q: Where should I park for the Chanthaboon Waterfront?
faq.a: The street through the community is narrow and hard for cars to pass each other. It's best to park around a temple lot or on a street outside the community and walk in, which is more convenient and avoids the congestion.
